title: The Unexpected Songbook
premise: Mirabel Okonkwo, drowning in café debt, agrees to pose as the girlfriend of Theo Ashford at his family's vineyard reunion — only to discover the Ashfords' fortune is built on a song catalog stolen from her late mother, a songwriter whose royalties were buried by a forged contract. As their fake romance turns real, Mirabel must choose between the loyalty Theo offers and the truth she owes her mother, while Theo must decide whether protecting his family means protecting its crimes. At the vineyard's first harvest festival, before the grapes come in, they publicly play her mother's recovered songbook and expose the decade-old forgery, choosing justice over inheritance. The book ends with the Ashford estate settling restitution, Mirabel's café saved by legitimate royalties, and the two of them sharing a first real date — no pretense required.
about_author: Astrid Blackwood is the pen name of a former music-rights paralegal who spent six years untangling disputed songbooks before turning to fiction full-time. She writes romance from a converted farmhouse in upstate New York, where she bakes far better bread than plot twists.

chapters.title: Three Payments from Gone
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A final notice arrives at her failing café on the same day her mother's tenth death anniversary does, and she burns a batch of memorial lemon tarts. When Theo Ashford — a college friend turned estranged heir — walks in asking an enormous favor, desperation makes her say yes. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into recklessness.

chapters.title: The Terms of the Lie
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Over contractually precise coffee, Theo explains the reunion: his grandmother demands he arrive with a serious partner or lose his seat on the estate board. He offers to cover Mirabel's debts; she insists on calling it a loan. Both rehearse their backstory like lawyers. Emotional beat: two guarded people negotiating intimacy as fine print.

chapters.title: Arrivals at Ashford Hollow
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The vineyard is beautiful and hostile: Theo's brother Marcus runs the estate like a fiefdom, and the family matriarch, Odette, sizes Mirabel up like a vintage that won't keep. A shared glance across the dinner table feels dangerously unscripted. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into the sense of being watched.

chapters.title: The Locked Music Room
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Sent to fetch napkins, Mirabel finds a locked room humming with a piano she recognizes — her mother's unfinished melody, 'Vine Light,' played from sheet music bearing someone else's name. She says nothing at dinner, but her hands shake. Emotional beat: recognition as vertigo; the lie begins consuming itself.

chapters.title: What Theo Almost Knew
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo catches Mirabel photographing the music room door and covers for her instinctively — then starts pulling his own threads, finding a 2015 rights transfer signed by his father weeks before his death. Marcus warns him off with a smile. Emotional beat: loyalty cracking under the weight of a question he can't unask.

chapters.title: Dessert Confessions
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. After a harvest-prep disaster, Mirabel and Theo bake together past midnight and drop the act: she tells him about her mother, the stolen songs, the forged contract; he admits he suspected his father's death was too convenient. They kiss like people out of alibis. Emotional beat: the fake relationship dies and something honest takes its place.

chapters.title: Odette's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Odette corners Mirabel, revealing she has known about the theft for years — she kept quiet to protect the estate, and offers Mirabel hush money shaped like a generous catering contract. Mirabel refuses, but Odette leaves her one gift: the location of the original songbook. Emotional beat: temptation met with fury, then resolve.

chapters.title: The Night Before Harvest
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Marcus discovers Theo's investigation and threatens to have Mirabel removed — and the café's debt called in through friendly banks. Theo chooses sides, burning his board seat in absentia and stealing the original songbook from the estate safe. Emotional beat: betrayal of blood for principle, paid in full.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, climax. Before the pickers descend, Mirabel takes the festival stage, plays 'Vine Light' from her mother's own handwritten pages, and reads the forged 2015 contract aloud to the assembled family and press. Marcus implodes; Odette, unexpectedly, corroborates. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into testimony — the rehearsed sentence finally spoken.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Months later: restitution restores her mother's name to the catalog, royalties save the café, and Theo arrives not as an heir but as a man with flour on his sleeves asking for a date with nothing fake about it. She says yes before dessert. Emotional beat: justice settled, love unguarded, timing finally right.
